speaker: gm
text:
Wendell Prout turns slowly on the sack hoist above the shut loft door. A pigeon watches from the beam, judging the workmanship. Below, a scrawny boy in boots far too large for him lobs gutter stones at the body. “Missed. Cob never misses. That one was warning.” A sharp-faced girl perched on the yard wall swears at him, then at the morning, in two languages and possibly a third.

The sergeant steps away from the gate, notebook open. “Sergeant Agnes Kell. The Captain says suicide. I’m not signing anything yet, investigator.” A stone clangs off the hoist hook. The pigeon lifts one foot, as if considering a complaint.

marks.note: The Captain has already called Wendell’s death suicide, but Kell is holding off on accepting that conclusion. The yard’s porters say the Captain’s judgment is suicide too.

speaker: player
text: Boy. Stop that.

speaker: gm
text:
Cob’s next stone stays in his fist. He looks you over, then glances at the sergeant.

“Cob was doing it before you got here.”

The girl on the wall gives a short, sharp laugh. “That’s his apology. It’s very nearly sincere.”

Kell taps her pencil once against the notebook. “He’s heard you, investigator.”

speaker: player
text: (I look up at the body and the knot.)

speaker: gm
text:
From below, the cord disappears over the beam and runs through a slot above the loft door. Prout’s body turns slowly beneath it; you can’t make out the knot from here.

Kell follows your gaze. “The porters couldn’t reach him. The loft door’s barred from inside. They tried it with a hook-pole.”

Cob has stopped throwing stones, but still holds one. The girl on the wall watches you, heels drumming against the brick.

speaker: player
text: (I try the loft door.)

speaker: gm
text:
The loft door stands high in the granary wall, shut fast. Its lower edge is well above your reach from the cobbles; the bar is on the other side. Kell watches you test it from beside the gate.

“That’s the loft door, investigator. The porters tried it with a hook-pole.”

From the wall, the girl in the shawl gives a dry snort. “You’ll need longer arms, dwarf.”

speaker: player
text: Way inside?

speaker: gm
text:
Kell looks from you to the high slot above the loft door. “The rope goes through there. The loft is on the other side.”

The girl in the shawl gives a shrug from the wall. “Big doors are locked. Unless you’ve got a key, you’re staying out here.”

marks.note: The granary’s big doors are padlocked, and the warden or the Purveyor’s under-purveyors hold the keys. You haven’t said you have one.

speaker: player
text: Who has key?

speaker: gm
text:
Kell answers without leaving her place by the gate. “The warden keeps the key. She’s at the palace, counting provisions. The runner came back with ‘After the Assembly.’”

Her pencil taps once against the notebook. “The porters’ ladders are locked inside. The yard was swept bare yesterday.”

The girl on the wall swings her heels, eyes fixed on you. “There’s no ladder here, if that’s what you’re asking. Unless you mean the water butt.” She glances toward it, then quickly back to Cob. “And I wouldn’t put that boy on a ladder. He’d charge you rent.”

speaker: player
text: (I roll the water butt under the door and climb.)

speaker: gm
text:
The full water butt is thirty-two feet off. You’re beside the loft door, and the butt hasn’t moved. Kell’s eyes follow your glance toward it.

“It’s in the corner, investigator. You’d have to roll it across the yard.”

Cob looks toward the loft door, and the stones in his fist stop clicking. The girl on the wall watches him, not you. The granary’s big doors remain padlocked; there’s no ladder in the swept yard. Behind the water butt, a board sits a little crooked against the wall.

speaker: player
text: (I go to the crooked board. Pull it.)

speaker: gm
text:
The loose board pulls away with a dry scrape. Behind it is a child-sized gap into darkness, smelling of grain dust and old sacking.

Cob goes very still. A stone slips from his fist and clicks on the cobbles.

“That’s Cob’s castle.”

Kell’s pencil pauses over her notebook. From the wall, the girl in the shawl swings down to the yard side, her eyes on Cob.

“Leave it, Brann.”

marks.note: You pulled away the board and uncovered Cob’s hidden place. The girl is asking you not to disturb it; you did that.

speaker: player
text: (I crouch to Cob's height.) Your castle. You saw.

speaker: gm
text:
Cob looks from the gap to you, then swallows. His eyes flick toward the boots.

“Cob sleeps where Cob likes.”

He edges toward the water butt, still watching you, and says nothing more. The girl in the shawl has gone quiet on the wall. Kell’s pencil waits above her open notebook.

speaker: player
text: Good boots. Whose?

speaker: gm
text:
Cob glances down at his oversized black boots, then back at you.

“Found ’em.”

The girl in the shawl shifts closer, her gaze fixed on you. Kell’s pencil rests above the open notebook.

speaker: player
text: (I look up at Prout's feet.)

speaker: gm
text:
Prout’s stockinged feet hang well above the cobbles. Cob’s eyes follow yours, then drop to his boots. He stamps once; the left boot gives a faint crackle.

“Good boots.”

The girl in the shawl watches him closely. Kell’s pencil rests above her open notebook.

speaker: player
text: (I hold out a copper.) Left boot. Trade.

speaker: gm
text:
Cob eyes the copper in your hand. His shoulders lift a fraction; the bravado returns.

“A copper? For a look at Cob’s boot? That’s a rich man’s copper. Two.”

He edges another step toward the water butt, keeping both boots firmly planted. The left one gives a faint crackle as he shifts.

“And no taking it off. You look from there.”

speaker: player
text: (Second copper.) Two. Show.

speaker: gm
text:
Cob snatches the second copper, then plants his feet and grins.

“Two coppers buys a look. Cob’s boots stay on.”

He turns his left boot outward and taps the leather with one knuckle. The stiff lining crackles faintly beneath it. From the wall, the girl in the shawl watches his hands.

“There. You’ve looked. Boots are still Cob’s.”

speaker: player
text: Not the boot. The paper.

speaker: gm
text:
Cob’s grin falters. His eyes flick to the boot, then to you.

“What paper?”

The girl in the shawl turns sharply toward him. Kell’s pencil stills.

The stiff lining gives a small crackle beneath the leather. As you indicate what you mean, Cob’s grip tightens around the boot.

“Mister Prout’s. He put something in there.”

He looks down at the boot, suddenly quiet. “Don’t take it off me.”

marks.note: You asked to see the paper in Cob’s boot, and he’s asking you not to take the boot off him.

speaker: player
text: Boots stay yours. Just the paper.

speaker: gm
text:
Cob holds your gaze a moment, then looks down at the boot.

“All right. Boots stay Cob’s.”

He crouches, works at the laces, and eases the left boot off. Keeping it clutched to his chest, he turns the opening toward you. A stiff, folded paper is tucked into the lining.

“That’s Mister Prout’s.”

speaker: player
text: (I take the paper. Read it.)

speaker: gm
text:
You unfold the paper. It’s a cut page from the Royal Granary Roll, its edges ragged where it was removed. Several wagons marked “lost to goblins” are listed against the King’s Road; beside each entry is the same countersignature: “J. Sallow, for the Royal Purveyor.”

Kell comes closer, reading over your shoulder. Her pencil moves. “Royal Granary Roll: King’s Road wagons, recorded lost to goblins. Countersigned, ‘J. Sallow, for the Royal Purveyor.’ Page recovered from the lining of Wendell Prout’s boot. Noted.”

Cob keeps the boot clutched to his chest. The girl in the shawl looks from the page to Kell’s notebook, and her fist tightens.

marks.note: The Royal Purveyor’s office supplies the palace with everything it needs, including grain, and manages wagons, carters and stores across the city.
You took the paper from Cob’s boot and read it. Kell is recording where you found it.
